sourceBaseline.interpretation: Compatibility evidence is preserved where safe; client-only bounds, silent filter behavior, fallback authentication and unbounded provider work are findings rather than production targets.

evidence.anchor: limit: Math.min(filters.limit ?? 10, 10), // Public API limit: max 10

targetBase.interpretation: Immutable post-A2.4 snapshot before provider extraction, request bounds, shared concurrency ownership, single-attempt transport and deterministic provider tests.

invariants.claim: The canonical rankings handler calls one injected MarketRankingsProviderPort and contains no direct TradingView construction or WebSocket enhancement.
Standalone and monolith runtimes each construct one bounded provider Arc from their existing shared TradingView service and inject that Arc into the router.
Anonymous rankings requests and successful provider pages are capped server-side at 10 rows, matching the pinned public client contract.
Authenticated rankings requests and successful provider pages are capped at 100 rows, matching the existing UI pagination vocabulary and provider maximum.
Rank offset, page and limit arithmetic is checked before provider work; accessible pagination totals exclude locked ranks and unsupported ranges fail validation.
One process-shared semaphore admits at most five concurrent provider calls and saturation fails fast with a sanitized 503.
Transient transport, 408, 429 and 5xx provider failures are retryable while permanent HTTP failures are not; no logical request performs more than three total attempts.
All provider attempts and backoff for a logical request are contained by one 30-second deadline; timeout cancellation releases the permit.
The live rankings adapter performs one raw HTTP attempt; it has no nested retry beneath the bounded decorator.
Provider response bodies, credentials and raw transport details do not reach ranking clients; 502, 503 and 504 classes remain distinguishable.
The live HTTP response body is capped at two MiB, successful pages cannot exceed the requested row count, and negative provider totals fail closed.
Successful fake-provider results preserve the existing card, rank and quarterly projection shape.
A2.5 does not claim authoritative paid access or strict authority-outage behavior; those remain the next identity dependency.
All A2.5 evidence is offline and in-process; no provider, identity, database, Redis, RPC, listener, browser or deployment action is authorized.

residualStops.claim: The monolith still owns canonical market routes and no gateway, Cloudflare, workload or DNS cutover is authorized or proven.
Legacy public aliases, API-key behavior, query closure, financial filters, country/sector normalization, envelopes, HEAD and wrong-method compatibility remain incomplete.
The identity ranking-offset service still returns free-plan authority for every wallet, so paid rank ranges are not proven.
Authenticated authority failures still silently fall back to free and can continue into provider work.
TradingView licensing, quota, schema compatibility, exchange/timezone normalization, observation time, freshness, cache age and stale semantics remain unproven.
The five-call budget is process-local; cross-replica quotas, adaptive throttling, circuit breaking and distributed cache behavior remain unproven.
Admin, repository, watchlist and other legacy TradingView call paths do not yet share the A2.5 rankings boundary.
The identity gRPC query has no authenticated service identity, owner binding, NetworkPolicy or immutable non-development image proof.
Identity still exposes unauthenticated emit/global stream paths and dormant historical SSE source remains pending archive cleanup.
Checked-in overlays still select pre-candidate images/configuration and health does not prove identity or market-provider readiness.
No typed BFF loader or responsive Dioxus loading, authoritative-empty, error, stale, filter, pagination, watchlist and entitlement journey consumes this contract.
No accepted real JWT, provider, identity, proxy, listener, browser, staging or fault-injection exercise exists.
No image publication, secret mutation, service restart, canary, rollback or production deployment is authorized by this contract.

requiredExecutionOrder: E01 Verify and commit the A2.5 provider port, request bounds, process-shared budget, retry/deadline owner and opaque failure contract.
E02 Make identity ranking offsets authoritative from backend plan assignments and fail authenticated authority errors before provider work.
E03 Authenticate analytics-to-identity service calls and keep global emit/stream paths unavailable until an owner-safe durable protocol exists.
E04 Lock query, filter, API-key, envelope, provenance, observation-time, freshness, cache and provider-commercial compatibility against the pinned source.
E05 Select one production market route owner and add explicit gateway or BFF routing without colliding with event analytics.
E06 Add the typed frontend BFF loader and Dioxus loading, authoritative-empty, error, stale, filter, sort, pagination, watchlist and entitlement states.
E07 Run hermetic full-story tests, then separately authorized disposable and staging exercises with observability, shadow parity and rollback evidence.
E08 Request production deployment authorization only after every residual STOP is closed.
